name: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)
description: SHAP is a unified approach to explain machine learning model predictions based on Shapley values from cooperative game theory. It provides locally accurate, consistent, and fair feature attributions that explain how each feature contributes to pushing the prediction away from the baseline (average prediction).

concept.shapleyValues: Game-theoretic approach: each feature's contribution is its marginal contribution averaged over all possible coalitions
concept.additiveProperty: Sum of SHAP values + baseline = prediction
concept.baseline: Expected value (average prediction over training set)
concept.marginalContribution: Change in prediction when feature added to coalition
concept.explanation: SHAP values distribute the prediction fairly among features based on their contribution in all possible feature combinations.

avoidWhen: When correlation between features makes interpretation difficult
Very large datasets for exact calculation

explainerType.impact: Different approximations for different model types

nsamples.impact: More samples = more accurate but slower

treeExplainer.description: Exact SHAP for tree models (XGBoost, LightGBM, sklearn trees)

properties.localAccuracy: SHAP values sum to difference between prediction and baseline
properties.missingness: Features not in model have SHAP value of 0
properties.consistency: If model changes so feature has higher impact, its SHAP value increases

calculation: Compute SHAP values for test samples
For TreeExplainer: uses efficient polynomial algorithm
interpretation: SHAP summary plot: global feature importance
SHAP dependence plot: feature value vs. SHAP value

complexity.treeExplainer: O(T × L × D) where T=trees, L=leaves, D=depth
complexity.scalability: TreeExplainer fast; KernelExplainer slow for many features

cons: Can be slow for large datasets
Interpretation requires care with correlated features

visualizations.summaryPlot: Beeswarm/dot plot of SHAP values per feature
